answer: Reputation-weighted thread inheritance. Each new identity seeds from a parent’s history but starts in a shallow lagoon of low-trust capacity: transaction throughput and matching priority scale with the length of a clean, time-stamped activity river, not with registration. Cloning forces the attacker to either spend real time sustaining each branch (the per-identity cost is elapsed honest activity plus the forgone value of any short-lived burst) or abandon branches before they mature. The curve makes N sybils cost roughly N × maturity-time, so identity count stops paying.
